messages:
maria: Heads up — customer `acme-inc` opened a high-severity ticket, getting sustained 429s for calls that should hit their Dedicated GPU pool. Started ~09:12 UTC and still happening. Autoscale didn't bring up more dedicated nodes and some traffic fell back to shared pools (cold).

sam: Can you paste a sample request id + tenant id? I'll pull logs and check control plane routing.

maria: Tenant: tenant-acme-01. Example request ids: req_01GZKJ2, req_01GZKJ3, req_01GZKJ8. They report spikes right after a deploy at 09:05.

alice: I pulled the control-plane policy-eval logs for tenant-acme-01 around those requests. Seeing policy evaluation result: `tier_key=Gold-Tier` but the routeset only has `gold` (lowercase). The normalization step returned null and eval fellthrough -> default pool. Snippet:```json
{"request_id":"req_01GZKJ2","headers":{"x-tenant":"tenant-acme-01","x-tier":"Gold-Tier"},"route_eval":"NO_MATCH","selected_pool":"default-shared-cold"}
```

ben: This looks like the header normalization / policy matcher bug we've seen before but not in this combination. The route matcher expects normalized token of `gold` or canonical labels; casing + hyphen makes the pattern not match. The fallback triggers sticky fallback behavior which doesn't count toward dedicated autoscale because it treats it as shared traffic.

charlie: Quick mitigation options: 1) patch a tenant override to map `Gold-Tier` -> gold in the control plane (short term); 2) patch the route matcher to normalize non-alphanum to dashes and lowercase (longer). I can apply the tenant override now if you want.

maria: Please do the tenant override, customer is getting 429s and billing complaints. What's the API call?

charlie: POST /controlplane/v1/tenants/tenant-acme-01/routes/overrides body:```json
{"match":{"header":"x-tier","value":"Gold-Tier"},"action":{"route_to":"dedicated-pool-01","priority":100}}
``` After apply, it should re-evaluate new requests immediately.

leo: FYI the autoscaler logic currently ties scales to `selected_pool` metrics; because traffic was misrouted to `default-shared-cold`, dedicated-pool metrics never rose so autoscale didn't kick. Once we route properly autoscaler should detect and spin up. We should also consider emitting a synthetic metric for tenant-level demand as a safety net.

sam: Applied the tenant override at 09:32 UTC and pushed a rule. Customer confirms reduced 429s at 09:36. Need follow-up: postmortem + permanent fix.

ben: Root cause summary for the ticket: control-plane header normalization bug for tier labels containing mixed case and punctuation -> route matcher missed dedicated route -> fallback to default shared pool -> autoscaler not triggered for dedicated -> user-facing 429s.

ingrid-bot: Alert: dedicated-pool-01 utilization spike observed 09:36 -> scaling event started. Incident ticket updated: #INC-8421.

maria: Action items: (1) eng-runtime/infra to implement robust header normalization and update matcher (ben + alice) (2) add tenant-level demand metric for autoscaler safety (leo) (3) run a targeted test with mixed-case tiers in staging (charlie) (4) customer comms + credit (support/sam). I'll open the PM.

ben: I'll start working on a small safe change to normalize headers (lowercase + strip non-alphanum -> replace with dash) and add unit tests. Plan to roll to staging today and prod tomorrow after validation.

alice: I'll extract the policy-eval logs and attach to the postmortem. Also will check whether other tenants have similar tier label variants to estimate blast radius.

sam: Noted. I'll follow up with ACME support thread and confirm they've seen steady success. Marking incident as "mitigated" for now. :thumbsup:
